A REST (Representational State Transfer) API is an internet service that provides a structured way for users to interact with web services and other APIs hosted on the server side of the internet. It allows developers to define HTTP methods, parameters, headers, and other metadata for an application using a protocol-independent API specification language known as JSON. This enables applications to communicate with each other without needing to know about the underlying implementation details of a particular API or service provider.

REST APIs are designed to be highly scalable and performant on their own without requiring changes from users. They follow standard HTTP methods such as GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, and others, making it easy for applications built around them to leverage the full range of capabilities offered by various services.
The most commonly used programming languages that can host REST APIs are JavaScript (Node.js), Python (Django or Flask), Java (Spring Boot), Ruby (Ruby on Rails), C# (ASP.NET Core), and others. These technologies provide a platform for building applications that interact with each other using a REST API, allowing them to communicate efficiently across the internet.
REST APIs are widely used in many areas such as software development, data processing, web services, and cloud computing. They facilitate easier communication between different parts of an application or system, enabling users to access the required resources without needing to know about the underlying implementation details of a particular service provider or server-side code.
